Description:
Settings for the terrain erosion noise filter.
Erosion creates branching gullies and ridges on the terrain.
Taken from Runevision's erosion filter: https://blog.runevision.com/2026/03/fast-and-gorgeous-erosion-filter.html
EnabledDescription: Whether this erosion noise filter is used or not.
StrengthDescription:
Strength of the erosion's effect on the terrain.
Higher strength values are super crazy, keep this between 0.0 and 0.25
SlopeResolutionDescription:
The size of the chunks, defined in blocks squared (so 8 gives a 8x8 chunk) which are used to create sampled terrain slopes for the erosion filter.
It can do these resolutions: 2 4 8 16 32 64
CellFrequencyDescription:
Frequency of the of voronoi cells. These cells are used to anchor and pivot the direction of the stripe erosion pattern.
More frequent cells mean smaller cells and therefore smaller gully & ridge stripes.
And vice-versa less frequent means larger cells and larger gullies & ridges.
OctaveCountDescription:
Number of octaves of the terrain erosion stripes. Works just like noise octaves where each successive octave is a smaller version of the previous.
More octaves give more complex erosion patterns.
DetailDescription:
Controls how much the smaller octave ridge and gulley stripes override the previous larger octaves.
Higher detail means that you get better defined small ridges/gulleys ontop of the larger ones.
Lower detail means that the larger ridges/gulleys define the stripe/wave shape more.
LacunarityDescription:
Size ratio between successive octaves.
0.5 means each octave's gullies/ridges are half the size of the previous octave.
BranchStrengthDescription:
How much smaller erosion octaves/branches are rotated away from the larger/previous octave/branch.
Higher creates a lot of v-like branching, lower gives a striated/parallel ll-like look.
ErosionSlopeSensitivityInitialOctaveDesc: Based on the pre-erosion terrain slope, how much erosion should be allowed to go through on the first octave.
ErosionSlopeSensitivitySuccessiveOctaves: Based on the erosion slopes from all the previous octaves, how much erosion on the current octave should be allowed to go through.
RidgeMapSensitivityInitialOctaveDescript: Based on the pre-erosion terrain slope, how much of the ridge shape/pattern should be allowed to go through on the first octave.
RidgeMapSensitivitySuccessiveOctavesDesc: Based on the ridge patterns/shapes from all the previous octaves, how much of the ridge shape/pattern on the current octave should be allowed to go through.
ErosionBoundaryRoundingInitialOctaveDesc: How rounded the boundary fade between flat (uneroded) and sloped (eroded) terrain is on the first octave.
ErosionBoundaryRoundingSuccessiveOctaves:
Based on the uneroded/eroded landform boundry fade from all the previous octaves, how much this multiplier should shrink/grow the boundry fade effect on the current octave.
Haven't really seen a need to adjust this since the erosion fade between erodable and unerodable landforms has been subtle so far.
But if you somehow set up the erosion to a state where the boundry fade is obvious, use this to roughen up the transition.
ErosionWaveMinFrequencyDescription: Minimum frequency multiplier on the flattest terrain. Prevents stripes from widening infinitely.
FullErosionWaveFrequencyAtThisSteepnessD: The slope magnitude at which erosion frequency is fully unaffected by the erosion fade out on flat slopes.
SteepnessEffectOnErosionWaveFrequencyDes: How much flat terrain slopes widen out the erosion waves, which effectively fades out the erosion effect.
GullyFadeOnFlatSlopesDescription: How much gullies fade out on flat slopes. Doesn't affect ridges.
GullyFadeSlopeThresholdDescription:
The slope magnitude below which gullies start fading out.
Slopes steeper than this threshold get full gully detail.
Slopes flatter than this have their gullies progressively faded.
SteepSlopeFadeStartDescription:
The slope magnitude at which erosion starts fading out on steep terrain.
Slopes gentler than this get full erosion. Slopes steeper than this have erosion progressively reduced.
SteepSlopeFadeEndDescription:
The slope magnitude at which erosion is fully faded out on steep terrain.
Slopes steeper than this get no erosion at all.
RidgeRoundingDescription:
How much to round/soften the tops of ridges.
More means smoother/wider, less means sharper.
GullyRoundingDescription:
How much to round/soften the bottoms of gullies.
More means smoother/wider, less means sharper.
